standard_prerequisites.name: A map out of a perfect complex into a bounded above complex of quasi-coherent modules vanishes in high degrees
The Hom groups, the Ext groups and the derived Hom are related by the standard identifications, and duality of a perfect complex relates the tensor expression to the derived Hom
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that conditions (2) to (6) are all equivalent.

standard_prerequisites.name: A perfect complex generating the derived category is a classical generator, and a property inherited by direct sums, summands and shifts and satisfying the two out of three property holds for all perfect complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Extends the equivalent conditions from the given generator to every perfect object, giving condition (7).

standard_prerequisites.name: The induction principle on quasi-compact opens reduces the converse to the affine case and a union step, and the truncation statement converts the vanishing against the Koszul complex into a truncation isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Organises the converse and supplies the truncation used in the union step.

core_obligations: Show that (1) implies (2) by shifting the argument to the vanishing of Hom from a perfect complex into a bounded above complex in high degrees (proof lines 10741-10744).

Record the equivalence of (2), (3), (4) by the identification of Hom, Ext and the derived Hom, the equivalence of (5) and (6) because cohomology is the cohomology of the derived global sections, and the passage between the two blocks by duality of the perfect generator (proof lines 10745-10754).

Take (7) implies (2) as clear, and conversely extend the conditions from the generator to every perfect object using that the property of having the derived Hom bounded above is inherited by direct sums, summands and shifts and satisfies the two out of three property, which the classical generator criterion converts into the statement for all perfect complexes (proof lines 10755-10766).

Prove that the equivalent conditions imply (1) by induction on quasi-compact opens, starting with the affine case: testing against the structure sheaf gives the vanishing of the cohomology in high degrees, and on an affine scheme the complex is determined by its derived global sections (proof lines 10767-10775).

For the union step, produce a perfect complex generating on the first open, cut the complement of that open inside the affine open by finitely many functions, form the Koszul complex on them and push it forward to a perfect complex supported on the complement, whose derived Hom into the given complex is bounded above (proof lines 10776-10797).

Use the second description of that auxiliary complex to get the vanishing of Hom from the Koszul complex into the restriction in high degrees, apply the orthogonal statement to obtain a truncation isomorphism with the direct image from the intersection, transfer the vanishing to the first open with the truncation statement, apply the induction hypothesis there, and conclude boundedness above on the whole scheme since the direct image of the open preserves the bounded above quasi-coherent complexes (proof lines 10798-10832).
proof_roadmap: The implications among (1) to (6) by the standard identifications and duality (proof lines 10741-10754).
Extension from the generator to all perfect complexes (proof lines 10755-10766).
Affine case of the converse via the structure sheaf (proof lines 10767-10775).
Union step: auxiliary perfect complex, truncation, induction, conclusion (proof lines 10776-10832).
